subject: Materials Science
title: Nanotechnology in Water Purification
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nanotechnology in Water Purification.

hook.text: Graphene oxide membranes filter salt from seawater — nanopores large enough for water, too small for salt.

buildup.text: Nano-filtration membranes use pore sizes of 1–10 nm — rejecting dissolved contaminants while passing pure water.

discovery.text: TiO₂ nanoparticles photocatalytically destroy organic pollutants and bacteria — sunlight-powered water purification.

twist.text: Silver and TiO₂ nanoparticles can leach from filters into drinking water — the purifier itself becomes a contaminant.

climax.text: Nano-enabled water filters are deployed in developing nations — clean water where infrastructure is scarce.

punchline.text: Nanomaterials making dirty water clean — life-saving tech at nanoscale.

quiz.question: How do graphene oxide membranes purify water?
options: They chemically react with and neutralize contaminants
Nanoscale pores allow water through while blocking larger salt ions and pollutants
They heat water to boiling to sterilize it
